clue.text: Novel from England with few exciting characters

indicators.note: exciting characters are stirred up, so the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A new book from England whose few characters are thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: ENGLAND and FEW together are rearranged, 'exciting' being the signal; 'from' and 'characters' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is new and unfamiliar, which is just what a newfangled gadget is.

clue.text: Being very loud at home raised a stink

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the run is read from the bottom up

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone making a racket at home caused a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns FFIN round, bottom to top in a down light. NIFF is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Niff is informal British English for an unpleasant smell, a synonym of stink.

clue.text: Sorcerer made a few hairs turn green on top

indicators.note: in a down light, on top places the turned piece above the other
turn tells us the word for green is flipped round

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced
a lock is a small tuft of hair

explanation.surface: A wizard made some hair on someone's head go green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' means inexperienced, not the colour; 'turn' and 'on top' work on it as a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlock is a male witch or wizard, so a sorcerer.

clue.text: My life — only I can take responsibility for it

definitions.text: My life — only I can take responsibility for it

parts.words: My life — only I can take responsibility for it
parts.note: a book of my life that only I can be responsible for is one written by its own subject

explanation.surface: Someone owning up that their life is their own responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A life story written by the person who lived it is, by definition, their own account.

clue.text: Gaudy decoration finally thrown out

indicators.note: out says a letter is put out of the decorating word

parts.note: a garnish is a decoration on food

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of thrown

explanation.surface: Showy ornaments were at last binned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N, the last letter of 'thrown', and 'out' removes it from GARNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means tastelessly bright and showy, a synonym of gaudy.

clue.text: Soldier in libel action over drug-is that desirable?

indicators.note: in places the soldier within the other letters
in a down light, over means the first piece sits above the drug
action on the word libel sets its letters in motion into a new order

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier sues for libel over drugs, asking whether that is wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' rearranges LIBEL to ELIBL; 'over' puts it above E, and GI goes 'in' to make ELI-GI-BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eligible person, especially a bachelor, is one regarded as a desirable match.

clue.text: That woman's a goddess

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone points out that a certain woman is divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Entangle close relative in tree when climbing

indicators.note: in places the relative inside the tree word
climbing in a down light means the tree is read upwards

parts.note: the lime is a tree, the linden
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: Getting a brother involved by having him up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns LIME into EMIL, and BRO goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to draw them into a conflict, entangling them in it.

clue.text: Thus sealant used to line well? Yes

indicators.note: the inner pieces line the inside of the word for well, sitting within it

parts.note: ably means well, competently
so means thus
lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints

explanation.surface: A plumber asks whether sealant should be used to line a well.
explanation.walkthrough: The lute here is a clay sealing paste, not the instrument; 'used to line' puts the pair within the word for well.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolutely is an emphatic way of saying yes in reply.

clue.text: Harbour master finally absorbed in this novelist

indicators.note: absorbed in says the letter is taken inside the other word

parts.note: to foster is to harbour, nurture

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of master

explanation.surface: A harbour master engrossed at last in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' is a verb here, not a port.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster wrote A Passage to India and Howards End.

clue.text: Nightmare as copper opens up in vehicle

indicators.note: the metal splits the following words apart by going between them

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman gets on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is the metal, not a police officer; it opens up IN + BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an evil spirit lying on sleepers, hence a nightmare.

clue.text: Firm's people introducing sturdy reinforcement

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the people word introduces the sturdy word, taking it in

parts.note: a nation is a people
solid means sturdy

explanation.surface: A company's staff bring in solid support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm's' gives only the firm; its 's is no letter. 'introducing' has the people take the sturdy word in.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolidation is the act of strengthening, a reinforcement.

clue.text: Burning curry, maybe, spilling on suit

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it, one example of combing

indicators.note: spilling sends the letters of on and suit tumbling out into a new order

explanation.surface: A hot curry spilt down someone's suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like the food; it is the grooming of a horse. 'spilling' rearranges ON SUIT to USTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Combustion is the process of burning.

clue.text: Predator bit head off chicken

indicators.note: biting the head off removes the first letter of the bird word

parts.note: a chicken is a fowl

explanation.surface: A hunter bit the head off a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are birds of prey, hunting predators.

clue.text: Having drunk this, traditionally one gets up to leave

definitions.text: Having drunk this, traditionally one gets up to leave

parts.words: Having drunk this, traditionally one gets up to leave
parts.note: a farewell drink taken before mounting a horse, so getting up into the saddle to go

explanation.surface: A last drink before a guest gets up and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' means mounts a horse, not rises from a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a drink offered to a rider already mounted before setting off.

clue.text: Square up to recruit

definitions.meaning: to ... a rival is to confront them
to ... staff is to hire them

explanation.definitionFit: Take on means both to tackle an opponent and to employ someone.

clue.text: Evening games thus given full coverage

definitions.text: Evening games thus given full coverage

parts.words: Evening games thus given full coverage
parts.note: night matches are bathed in a flood of light, coverage meaning lighting rather than broadcasting

explanation.surface: Night matches get complete television coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Night games are played under powerful lamps that light the whole pitch.

clue.text: One man suffers with endless noise, a problem at night

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: these letters suffer a battering into a new order
endless drops the final letter of noise

explanation.surface: A man suffers because of a constant racket at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts NOISE to NOIS; 'suffers' rearranges I, MAN and NOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is inability to sleep, a nocturnal complaint.

clue.text: Respectful at all times during split

indicators.note: during places the time phrase within the other word

parts.note: rent means torn, split
ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: Polite throughout a separation.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect.

clue.text: Bribable, holding tenner by the edges — it's on the low side

indicators.note: holding says the bribable word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: venal means open to bribery

indicators.note: the edges of tenner are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A corrupt official holding a ten-pound note, hiding it low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the edges' takes T and R from 'tenner', a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventral means relating to the belly, the underside of an animal.

clue.text: Weapon is discovered in failed plot

indicators.note: discovered in says the word is found inside the other letters
a failed plot falls apart, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gun is found after a botched conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' gives PTOL from the plot, and 'discovered in' sets the two letters of 'is' after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a handgun, a weapon.

clue.text: Making neat drawing in which I had featured

indicators.note: featured in says the I had piece appears within the other word

parts.note: drawing a game is tying it
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: Tidying a picture that I had appeared in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' means finishing level, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidying is making something neat and orderly.

clue.text: Sumptuous stroke secures six

indicators.note: secures means the stroke word holds the number inside it

parts.note: a lash is a stroke of a whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A batsman's stroke gets a six.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: stroke is a whip blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means richly luxurious, a synonym of sumptuous.

clue.text: Vessel anchored in Bournemouth

indicators.note: anchored in says the letters lie fixed inside the place name

explanation.surface: A ship moored at the seaside town of Bournemouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Bournemouth is an English south-coast resort; 'Vessel' suggests a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, a vessel.

clue.text: Real goose, reading out publicity material

indicators.note: reading out means the phrase is voiced and what we hear is entered

parts.note: proper means real and a gander is a male goose

explanation.surface: A genuine goose reads out an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic accent, 'proper gander' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is material spread to promote a cause or point of view.

clue.text: Dish left in cooler

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the cooling device

parts.note: a fan cools

explanation.surface: A dish left in the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' suggests a fridge but is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open tart, a dish.

clue.text: Questionable behaviour, working at two forms of transport

parts.note: a car is one form of transport
Ry is short for railway, a second form of transport
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Misbehaving while operating two vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A carry-on is a fuss or shady goings-on, informal British for dubious conduct.

clue.text: First fellow leaves cap on roof — bring it inside

indicators.note: inside places the word it within the rest
leaves says the fellow's letter departs from the roof ornament

parts.note: a finial is an ornament capping a roof or gable

explanation.surface: A man loses his hat on the roof and must bring it in.
explanation.walkthrough: A finial is a roof ornament; 'leaves' removes the fellow, giving INIAL, and 'bring it inside' needs 'bring' as a mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first, at the beginning.

clue.text: Colourless soft drink

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for soft
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A pale soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale means lacking colour.

clue.text: With a measure of speed sister, say, grabbed weapon

parts.note: Mach one is the speed of sound, written Mach I

indicators.note: grabbed means the sister holds the example abbreviation

parts.note: a nun is a sister
eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A nun at speed grabbed a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a measure of speed' gives MACH I, I being one.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine gun is an automatic firearm.
